subject: radio telescope
title: What If Your Town Banned Wi-Fi and Cell Phones? One in America Does

scenes.text: What if your town banned Wi-Fi and cell phones? One in America does, on purpose.
scenes.keywords: small town main street West Virginia

scenes.text: Since 1958, about 13,000 square miles of West Virginia have been the National Radio Quiet Zone, created by the FCC.
In the middle sits the Green Bank Telescope, the largest fully steerable radio telescope on Earth. Its dish could hold two acres of land.
It listens for energies weaker than a single snowflake landing. So within ten miles: no cell service, no Wi-Fi, no Bluetooth, no cordless phones.
Staff patrol a 20-mile radius every week hunting stray signals. Microwaves near the telescope sit inside steel boxes.
Green Bank's population is about 143. Some of them came for the silence: people who believe wireless signals make them ill.

description:
What if Wi-Fi and cell phones were banned where you live? In Green Bank, West Virginia, they are: the town sits at the centre of the 13,000-square-mile National Radio Quiet Zone, created by the FCC in 1958 to protect the Green Bank Telescope, the largest fully steerable radio telescope in the world.
Within ten miles, cell service, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and cordless phones are out; staff patrol a 20-mile radius for stray signals, and microwaves near the telescope live in steel boxes.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: The telescope is as tall as the Washington Monument and still has to be protected from a microwave oven. Could you live a year with no phone signal?
